learningObjectives: Explain how logging and monitoring support production applications.
Identify useful application metrics and log levels.
Design a basic observability workflow for diagnosing application behavior.

activities.title: Observability Signals
activities.instruction: Explore the main signals used to understand application behavior.

content.concept: Observability commonly combines logs, metrics, and traces. Each signal provides a different view of what the application is doing and helps investigate production behavior.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Detailed timestamped records of application events.
Numerical measurements such as latency, request rate, and resource usage.
Records that help follow a request across components or services.
Notifications generated when configured conditions indicate a potential problem.

activities.title: Log Level Selection
activities.instruction: Choose the most appropriate log level for the scenario.

content.concept: Common logging levels communicate different degrees of detail and severity. DEBUG is useful for detailed diagnostic information, INFO for normal application events, WARN for concerning conditions, and ERROR for failures.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

choices: Detailed variable values needed during development debugging → ERROR

activities.title: Monitoring Metrics
activities.instruction: Explore which metrics reveal application health.

content.concept: Request rate, latency, error rate, and resource utilization provide quantitative signals about application traffic, responsiveness, failures, and infrastructure health.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Measures how many requests the application receives over time.
Measures how long requests take to complete.
Measures the proportion or number of failed requests.
Shows resource consumption that may indicate capacity or performance problems.

activities.title: Incident Investigation
activities.instruction: Arrange a practical workflow for investigating a production issue.

content.concept: Troubleshooting combines alerts, metrics, logs, and traces to establish when a problem started, understand its impact, identify its likely cause, and verify the resolution.
